newsitem.title: USA: America Online sets marketing pact with CUC.
newsitem.headline: America Online sets marketing pact with CUC.

text.p: America Online Inc. and the huge marketing company CUC International Inc. Tuesday agreed to a deal to put CUC's shopping, travel and other online services on the AOL network.
The nation's largest online service will receive at least $50 million under the three-year marketing agreement, which could be worth more because of revenue sharing, the companies said.

Under the deal, CUC will allow AOL's 8 million subscribers to buy goods and services at discounts through CUC's Internet site and its Shoppers Advantage, Travelers Advantage, Auto Vantage and other clubs, the companies said.

CUC, a direct marketing powerhouse, last month agreed to a $10.9 billion merger with HFS Inc., a franchiser whose brands include Ramada Inn, Century 21 Real Estate, Howard Johnson, Avis and Coldwell Banker.

The company, based in Stamford, Conn., offers coupon books as well as traveler and shopper clubs to its members, who pay an annual fee to buy goods and services at discount rates. CUC has recently been trying to develop more online revenue, and the agreement with AOL is a step in that direction.

AOL, based in Dulles, Va., is in a battle with Compuserve, Microsoft Network, Prodigy and other online providers to lure and retain subscribers. One way the companies have been trying to win customers is by offering exclusive content.
Another way is to offer consumers products and services online since online providers typically get fees based on the transactions.
The marketing pact with CUC could also help AOL win about a million new subscribers a year, the companies said, based on CUC's promotions, direct mail and telemarketing activities.
"Our agreement with CUC demonstrates the enormous value of our member base to sophisticated marketing and consumer service providers," said Bob Pittman, chief executive officer of AOL Networks.
"The agreement furthers our drive to accelerate the growth of revenues from online advertising, e-commerce and transactions, which are key to AOL's business success."

The pact comes despite uncertainty over the direction of online commerce for consumers. The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that International Business Machines Corp. is preparing to close World Avenue, its World Wide Web-based shopping mall unveiled only a year ago.
AOL's stock rose $1.25 to $58.50, while CompuServe climbed 50 cents to $24.125 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
